correctness.rationale: The exact core-forcing lemma is proved from private-leaf adjacency and the no-isolates condition for an induced perfect matching. Selected leaves force their incident matching edges and the remaining core has a perfect matching precisely when the paired set exists. The coefficientwise inequality is termwise in induced supports. Unique induced perfect matchings are equivalent to absence of even cycles by alternating symmetric difference and two cycle matchings. For forests the Leibniz expansion has only fixed points and transpositions and yields the determinant with correct signs; a real-symmetric spectral theorem proves imaginary zeros. The packaged verify.py independently checks all 1099 simple graphs on 1..5 vertices and four larger examples, but all-order truth rests on the written proof.

value.rationale: The statement detects an exact graph-theoretic boundary: an even cycle and only an even cycle causes overcounting when matchings are projected to paired-dominating vertex sets under full whiskering. Beyond a known scalar parameter, the forest case gives the entire domination generating function as an adjacency characteristic determinant evaluated on the imaginary axis, yielding spectral recovery and precise optimizer multiplicities. This is a structural, motivated comparison of classical graph-polynomial invariants, not a renamed scalar or arbitrary finite slice.
